ending: Hal ends the book at the dragon-contest site after saving Besal from an external Beastborn possession. The undercover illusionist's false battle buys time for Hal to restore Besal's scarscape, where Hal and Besal mortally wound the rival. Besal then dissolves into star-filled mist that restores Hal, leaving his survival or transformation uncertain. Hal subsequently destroys the fleeing extension with dragon essence. The tyrant white remains alive after the possessed Besal defeats her, while the gold dragon is nearing defeat when the narrative leaves their contest and the final dragon-oath terms remain unsettled. Hal's restored monster core is functional, but hollow essence, Oversoul chains, and repeated founder-sigil backlash still endanger him. Brightsong is growing under Noth, Ashera, Elora, Vorax, and its council, with loyal kobolds sheltered there, but winter food preservation and materials remain tight. Rinbast is still protected from direct conflict until a Primacy Trial, and his archmage and Kinslayers are approaching. The injured court mage remains guarded because his loyalty and condition are uncertain.
in_short: After returning Brightsong's missing allies, Hal builds a council and enters Frostmourne to recover Elora's severed soul and save the gold dragon's imprisoned daughter. Elora regains Wild's Master, but Hal's use of hollow essence nearly destroys him. The Mage King and Dream kindred restore his defective Beastborn class with a monster core and reveal a wider conflict among bearers of his soul. Hal escapes Aldim's moon, defeats but spares the tyrant white, reunites her with the fractured dungeon core, frees her father, and shelters loyal kobolds. He challenges Rinbast for Beastborn Prime while Brightsong prepares for incoming Kinslayers. During a contest to bind both dragons by oath, hostile agents possess Besal. An undercover founder conceals the real struggle while Hal restores Besal's inner realm, where Hal and Besal mortally wound the rival. Besal dissolves into Hal and revives him, after which Hal destroys the fleeing extension. Besal's fate, the dragon oath, the Primacy Trial, and Brightsong's defense remain unresolved.

recaps.text: Previously: Hal became a Beastborn founder in Aldim and established Brightsong and the Bravers Guild in the Shiverglades. His closest allies include his inner counterpart Besal, his partner Noth, Ashera, Elora, Durvin, Angram, Mira, Lurklox, and his mimic companion Vorax. Hal's group has faced threats tied to dungeons, other worlds, and the unusual nature of his own class while trying to turn Brightsong into a lasting refuge.

So far: Hal has returned to Brightsong with the allies recovered by the recent gateway quest. The rescue brings new levels and abilities, but also troubling consequences: his eyes have changed, Dark Weave Mana is interfering with recovery, and the Draxt remains chained beneath the settlement. Several returnees have lost the soul portions that held entire classes. Durvin reveals that he is an exiled king but commits himself to building Brightsong before pursuing his clan or throne. Ashera accepts Royal Guard as a replacement class and forms a private Unity bond with Hal, while Elora and Durvin refuse replacements because they want their original powers restored. Hal responds to the settlement's vulnerability by delegating authority. Rondo becomes head clerk, Lurklox treasurer, and Ashera oversees internal order, while Noth remains responsible for external defense. Brightsong now has a working council, but housing, defenses, food, and the watched dungeon remain urgent problems.

So far: Brightsong's recovered leaders are rebuilding both themselves and the settlement. Hal has organized paired civic roles so that no essential responsibility depends on one person. Ashera becomes his envoy as well as a Royal Knight Commander, gaining limited authority to advise and represent him. The settlement delays a valuable inn because its residents still need housing before winter. Scarce labor, timber, stone, and food force Athagan and Barden to compromise: a quarry will improve material supply, while a basic interior wall will slow animals or hidden threats from the valley. The new barrier is only a delaying measure, not protection against a determined assault. Barden and Athagan continue to share construction authority despite competing priorities. Hal's transformed mana sapling is alive but weakened, and the ancient dungeon remains under observation. The lost class-bearing soul fragments beneath Brightsong have not been recovered, leaving Elora and Durvin diminished even as the council begins functioning.

So far: Brightsong's builders confirm that the settlement cannot expand safely without more raw materials and a durable source of food. Barden gives his son independent control of production while continuing the longhouse work, and Noth and Elora replace an aggressive monster-clearing proposal with a layered plan of fallback defenses. Hal then learns why the gold dragon remains imprisoned beneath Brightsong: leaving would also release the dragon's dangerous daughter, a tyrant white. The weakening prison appears connected to the return journey that severed several allies' classes. Elora's missing Wild's Master soul fragment may now be inside the daughter's dungeon. The gold dragon refuses to have his daughter killed, so Hal accepts a nonlethal rescue mission that could also restore Elora and free a powerful ally. Brightsong must prepare for an expedition into the unknown prison-dungeon.

So far: Hal equips a six-person expedition for extreme cold and leaves Lurklox behind to support construction, complete the inner wall, and investigate why neighboring tribes avoid the valley. Noth develops ice-adapted slimes, while Hal formally bonds Vorax as his monster familiar. The gold dragon explains that an awakened dungeon can expel defeated visitors rather than kill them permanently, making restored dungeons valuable for training and resources, but his daughter's prison is not yet safe. Hal accepts the quest to save the tyrant white as well as recover Elora's class. The party enters Frostmourne and reaches a frozen mountain route. Its first trap uses glittering motes to enthrall them while ice seals their bodies. Hal breaks free, and Ashera uses carefully controlled fire to wake the others and burn a route through the blocked passage. Retreat is uncertain, and the expedition has already learned that Frostmourne attacks thought and attention as readily as the body.

So far: Frostmourne divides and exhausts the rescue party. A broken bridge forces Hal to fly companions across an immense cavern above a waking monster. Ratlike attackers wear uniforms tied to Elora's past, and Hal discovers that they yield painful hollow essence rather than ordinary monster essence. Elora freezes when the cavern monster embodies her guilt over a fallen companion, but the party refuses to abandon her. Her light helps destroy it. Both the altered terrain and its inhabitants appear shaped by Elora's memories, and absorbing more hollow essence keeps harming Hal. The party moves forward after the victory without yet understanding the dungeon's increasingly personal challenges.

So far: Hal becomes separated inside Elora's convent nightmare and meets real kobolds who serve the tyrant white. They report that a speaking jewel began corrupting their home. Hal learns that their memories can weaken Elora's imposed illusion, while his own hollow essence can tear through its walls and guardians at increasing physical cost. By presenting himself as Bright Eyes of the Moon and claiming the gold dragon sent him, he wins support from rival clans and advances toward their ruler. Elsewhere, Ashera, Noth, Mira, Angram, Elora, and Vorax endure manifestations drawn from Elora's trauma. Hal offers the kobolds sanctuary in Brightsong if the dungeon can no longer protect them, creating a settlement-wide obligation and a quest to prevent at least one clan's extinction. As the illusions intensify, his repeated absorption of hollow essence makes him more powerful, aggressive, and unstable. He travels with the kobold clans toward the tyrant white's lair, recognizing how her protection has allowed them to survive and develop.

So far: The tyrant white allows Hal to remove the corrupting soul fragment and promises not to harm his people, but the dungeon's nightmare continues. Elora confronts distorted versions of Rinbast, her mother, and Hal as a future tyrant. Angram and Vorax are lost while defending her within the dungeon. Hal uses his Unity bond to cross the warped space and save Ashera and Noth, but hollow essence begins fracturing his body and judgment. His uncontrolled power creates false allies and threatens Aldim with instability. At the final trial, Elora must choose between a false prize and protecting Hal from the monster she fears he could become. She chooses Hal, causing her true soul to return. Wild's Master is restored at greater strength, and she accepts Hal as a trusted friend rather than a future tyrant she is responsible for preventing. Hal collapses after the effort. Elora's central recovery is complete, but the exhausted survivors remain inside Frostmourne with the tyrant white nearby.

So far: The wounded tyrant white grants the exhausted party a temporary truce, then an unknown interdimensional force removes Hal while everyone sleeps. Without him to verify their identity, the dragon conscripts Elora, Ashera, and Noth. Hal wakes with an interdimensional mage, who explains that the defective Beastborn class and absorbed dungeon essence are destroying his soul. Beastborn was not the safer class Hal was meant to receive, and continued use would eventually transform him into something else while also threatening Besal. Hal refuses a likely return to Earth because Aldim is now his home. When a Grey Arbiter orders his existence ended as a source of causation errors, the interdimensional mage invokes kindred judgment. The vessel reveals the Kindred of Dream, which knows the mage and questions why it has been summoned. Hal's companions remain under the tyrant white's control, and nothing is yet known about the rules or result of the judgment.

So far: The Dream kindred confirms that Hal's Beastborn class is missing its intended monster core, ranks, and evolutions, allowing hollow dungeon essence to poison his damaged soul. Hal chooses restoration over an experimental dungeon class. On Aldim's first moon, the kindred implants an unranked monster core and frees several weaker essences, stopping the immediate class failure without removing the deeper corruption. A journey through Hal's memories reveals that dungeon magic did not create the original wound. The founder who brought him to Aldim caused a transference paradox involving multiple bearers of Hal's soul, including an undamaged Beastborn counterpart. Hal receives the Beastborn Chronicles and a quest to confront his other selves, resolve the chains on his Oversoul, and pursue Beastborn Prime. The immediate repair gives him a way to train, but most of his essence remains locked behind hollow restraints. His companions are still stranded in Frostmourne, and Hal is now isolated on the moon with only limited shelter and an uncertain route home.

So far: Stranded on Aldim's moon, Hal studies his restored monster core. Golem essence grants tremendous strength but destabilizes the core unless he circulates it through a closed bodily path, while shadow essence provides stealth and speed. He cannot yet combine essences safely. In Brightsong, Elora's familiar attempts a settlement-enhancing brew with Mira, Vorax, Agda, and local crafters. The work reaches its aging stage despite dangerous magical imbalances. Then an unexplained force pulls the familiar and Vorax through the town hall roof and into the sky. Hal remains separated from Besal and unable to reach the distant Memoria crystal. Escape, reunion with his allies, and safe control of the new core all remain unresolved.

So far: Hal claims sigils from a defeated counterpart and accepts a Beastborn Prime rite against Rinbast, the strongest bearer of his soul in Aldim. Locked Struggle prevents either founder from directly harming the other until a pivotal Primacy Trial. The missing familiar and Vorax arrive on the moon through a recall device, bringing evidence of enormous crystals and hostile beings between worlds. With the familiar's help, Hal learns spirit-based primordial crafting and reproduces the chamber's air stone. Because each copy only functions near another, he lays a chain of breathable pockets toward the Memoria crystal. The alien creatures along the route are far beyond his level, so Hal creates unstable essence bombs that draw rival groups into fighting. Failing air pockets force a desperate sprint. Wounded and nearly out of oxygen, he swings past the final monsters, reaches the crystal, and touches it as he collapses. Escape and the condition of the allies in Frostmourne remain unknown.

So far: The Memoria crystal returns Hal to the Fathomways, where he finds Besal alive but fading and unable to use the network. Hal reaches Brightsong, stabilizes his restored core, and immediately returns to Frostmourne for his conscripted allies. He attacks the tyrant white, defeats her without killing her, and resists the strain that nearly drives him to drain her completely. Hal then discovers that a fragment of the fractured dungeon core has empowered, trapped, and aggravated the dragon. He bridges that fragment back to the larger core, freeing her from the dungeon while preserving her responsibility for exploiting his companions. Hal evacuates Ashera, Elora, Noth, and the unconscious dragon, then honors his earlier promise by offering refuge to loyal kobold clans. With their help, he breaks the gold dragon's remaining confinement. The father is freed, the daughter survives in a weakened state, and Hal earns a boon after completing the rescue. Brightsong must now absorb the kobolds and decide what relationship it will have with both dragons.

So far: Hal proposes an oath binding both dragons to Brightsong, then explains his restored monster core and moon journey to Noth. He uses a quest reward and the ancient dungeon to reduce the hollow obstruction separating him from Besal. Unable to reunite directly, Hal creates a spirit-filled pseudocore that gives Besal temporary solidity, though the effect is already fading. Their immediate priority becomes preparing for Rinbast and the unknown Primacy Trial. Elsewhere, the undercover illusionist joins a mage and two suspected Kinslayers traveling toward the Shiverglades, intending to betray them if doing so helps Rinbast's rival. In Merkmire, a former mayor accepts forbidden transpositional travel to warn Hal. She is chosen because Hal knows her and because her movement will not publicly expose the covert network supporting him. Brightsong is growing, but the warning establishes that a Kinslayer force is already on its way while Hal's dragon oath, core training, and Besal's separation remain unsettled.

So far: Hal and Noth turn a lake near Brightsong into both a food source and a training ground. A huge armored fish satisfies Hal's obligation to Elora's familiar and reveals a possible answer to the settlement's shortages. Hal dissolves its bones into temporary essence, builds a canoe, pier, and fishing structure, and discovers that bone crafting can strengthen his monster core while creating useful infrastructure. During this work, he recognizes that he loves Noth. New homes, minor structures, roads, and early farms show Brightsong's growth. Lurklox calls Hal back to Town Hall after the former Winstrom mayor reaches the settlement in visible distress. She has traveled to warn Brightsong about approaching Kinslayers, but has not yet delivered that warning to Hal.

So far: Brightsong approaches self-sufficiency through new longhouses, farms, production buildings, fishing, and Hal's bone crafting, but food preservation, iron, winter crops, and ranger coverage remain serious constraints. The injured court mage stays under guard because Shades Blight could make him dangerous, while Ashera and Angram monitor him and the perimeter. Hal orders an inn and workshop and continues preparing the settlement for Rinbast's Kinslayers. The gold dragon and his daughter agree to consider Hal's oath only through a draconic contest. Such an oath can endure through lineages and could bind both dragons to protect Brightsong's mana tree, but the tyrant white rejects the obligation. Hal accepts the contest against both dragons because success could secure the settlement and eventually provide dragonfire useful against the Blight. Noth cannot participate and strongly opposes the danger, but accepts his choice. The dragons break out of their lair and take flight, beginning a struggle whose exact oath terms will be determined through draconic law.

So far: Hal begins the draconic contest at a severe disadvantage because Noth cannot participate and both dragons can attack him together in the air. He briefly shifts the fight by stunning the tyrant white, damaging the gold dragon's wing, breaking his defenses, and using dragon essence to answer their roars. The effort consumes his spirit, while an unexplained loss of strain leaves him increasingly vulnerable. A young oracle separately uses rune-marked stones to steady a fading shadowy counterpart connected to Hal, though the procedure turns ominous as the stones change color. Hal's apparent progress against the dragons then collapses when the benefit from an earlier drink expires and a sugar-crash affliction impairs his movement and recovery. The dragons admit that they allowed him to take the drink as part of a plan to exhaust him rather than risk the destruction of an unrestricted battle. Hal is close to defeat, but the gold dragon says the contest will still produce an oath connecting both dragons to Brightsong while limiting damage to the settlement's mana tree and the surrounding region.

Hal enters the dragon contest and briefly incapacitates the tyrant white while wounding the gold dragon, but the pair have planned to outlast him after allowing him to consume a drink whose crash weakens him. The resulting oath is still expected to bind them to Brightsong, though its final form remains unsettled. At the same time, Rinbast's archmage and Kinslayers seize Besal through a hostile Beastborn extension. The undercover illusionist covertly uses a false battle to occupy the possessor's senses. Hal abandons surrender to the dragons and reaches Besal's mind with founder sigils. A direct reunion is too dangerous, so Hal restores Besal's scarscape and helps him fight the invader. Together they trap and mortally wound the rival despite severe wounds and escalating sigil backlash. Besal then dissolves into star-filled mist that revitalizes Hal, leaving his fate uncertain rather than confirming his death. Hal destroys the fleeing extension and promises to answer the remaining hostile Beastborn. Brightsong's defenders remain active, but Rinbast, the incoming Kinslayers, the Primacy Trial, the dragon oath, and Hal's deeper Oversoul damage are all unresolved.
